section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section clarifies that the precise question of the maamar is why the guarding of the soul's lamp depends on the lamp of Torah, particularly regarding souls of Atzilus.
section.t: And the explanation of the matter in more detail:
One must preface that the precision in the maamar—why they are
[the guarding of the lamp of the soul and the guarding of the lamp of Torah]
dependent upon each other—is
because "you have guarded My lamp" is not only that a person does not transgress G-d forbid a commandment of the Torah, but that he fulfills the commandments of the Torah21,
and therefore it is precise: why are they dependent upon each other?
For that the guarding of the lamp of the soul depends on one not transgressing G-d forbid a commandment of the Torah
is
because when one transgresses G-d forbid a commandment of the Torah, a blemish is caused in the soul.
And the precision in the maamar is that the guarding of the lamp of the soul depends on the fulfillment of the Torah22.
And one must add,
that the precision in the maamar is primarily regarding souls of Atzilus.
For regarding souls of BY"A
(which are the majority of souls)
one could say that the guarding of the lamp of the soul depends on the lamp of Torah because for them, the body and the animal soul conceal and obscure the soul,
therefore the guarding of the lamp of their soul is through the fulfillment of Torah and mitzvos
(as above in section 2),
and the precision and question in the maamar is primarily regarding souls of Atzilus,
for since for them the soul is revealed,
why do they need the lamp of Torah?

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section explains that the soul's lamp is its self-nullification, and complete nullification is achieved specifically through fulfilling the commandments, which are G-d's essential will.
section.t: And based on this, one must understand what is said in the maamar, that the guarding of the lamp of the soul is through the guarding of the lamp of Torah because "these are the names of the children of Israel that stand in the merit of these testimonies, statutes, and judgments"—
for seemingly,
that Israel stands in the merit of the Torah and mitzvos is that through fulfilling Torah and mitzvos they are elevated to a more exalted level23
(but the level of the souls of Israel in their own essence is seemingly not dependent on the Torah),
and the meaning of "if you guard My lamp, I will guard your lamp" is that the guarding of the lamp of the soul
(i.e., the level of the lamp of the soul in its own essence24)
is through the guarding of the lamp of Torah.
And this must be explained according to the statement of the Zohar25
cited in Tanya26,

that just as the light of a lamp does not shine and is not held in the wick without oil, so too the Shechinah does not rest upon the body of a person, which is likened to a wick, except through good deeds, which are likened to oil.
And it is explained in Tanya27,
that the reason for this is that
(the indwelling of the Shechinah upon the body of a person is specifically through the fulfillment of the commandments
(good deeds),
and)
his soul alone, which is a part of G-d above, is not sufficient to serve as oil for the wick,
for the soul of a person,
even when he is a completely righteous person serving G-d with fear and love in delights,
is not utterly nullified in existence,
rather it is a thing in itself, one who fears G-d and loves Him.
But the commandments, which are the innermost aspect of His will,
the life-force within them is not a separate entity at all, rather it is unified and included in His will.
And therefore the indwelling of the Shechinah upon the body of a person is specifically through the fulfillment of the commandments,
for the matter of the indwelling of the Shechinah in any thing is that that thing is included in the light of G-d and is utterly nullified in existence to Him,
for then specifically the One G-d dwells, is revealed, and shines in it.
And based on this, one can explain that the guarding of the lamp of the soul is through the guarding of the lamp of Torah,
for the matter of the lamp of the soul is its self-nullification28,
and the perfection of the soul's self-nullification
(utter nullification in existence)
is through the fulfillment of the commandments.
And this is that the lamp of the soul is called "your lamp"
(of the person)
and the lamp of Torah and mitzvos is called "My lamp"
(of the Holy One, blessed be He),
for the self-nullification of the soul
(in its own right)
is not ultimate nullification—"your lamp" of the person,
and the lamp of the commandments, which is the innermost aspect of His will, is "My lamp" of the Holy One, blessed be He.
And through a person fulfilling the commandments,
this nullification is drawn also into the soul,
"I will guard your lamp"29.

section.sectionSummaryBrief: This section connects the maamar to Shavuos, explaining that the elevation achieved through Torah and mitzvos parallels the new level of Israel revealed at the giving of the Torah, which includes a love of nullification inherited from the Patriarchs.
section.t: And to note,
that the aforementioned maamar is related to the holiday of Shavuos.
For in addition to the fact that the portion of Beha'aloscha
(the beginning of the maamar)
is read after the holiday of Shavuos30,
it is recorded at the beginning of the maamar that it is related to the discourse "Vayedaber Anochi"31.
And based on this, one could say,
that what is explained in the maamar, that through the fulfillment of Torah and mitzvos an elevation is made in the soul,
is analogous to the elevation of Israel that was renewed at the giving of the Torah.
And the matter is,
that the natural love in every Jew to be attached to G-d and not to separate from Him in any way, even with actual self-sacrifice, existed even before the giving of the Torah,
for this love is an inheritance for us from our forefathers.
And according to what is said in Tanya32
that this—that the forefathers bequeathed to every Jew this love—is related to the fact that the forefathers are themselves the Merkavah33,
for the matter of the Merkavah is that it is nullified to the rider
[for that the movement of the chariot
(the horses)
is according to the will of the rider is not because they want to have a connection to the rider
(like the aforementioned natural love, which is the desire that he be attached to G-d)
but because of their self-nullification to the rider],
one could say,
that in the natural love that comes as an inheritance from the forefathers, who are themselves the Merkavah, is included
(in a concealed way)
also the love that is in the category of self-nullification34,
where one wants nothing for himself at all, and all his desire is that there be a revelation of G-dliness in the world35
and that the intention of the dwelling place36
for Him, blessed be He, in the lower realms be completed.
